_readme: Creative specs library. Add an object to `specs` to extend. Fields: id (unique), format (one of `formats`), name, w/h (pixels, omit for audio), fileTypes, maxFileSize, duration, notes, source, verify (true = platform- or vendor-specific, check current specs before trafficking).

specs.name: Medium Rectangle
specs.notes: The most widely available display unit. Works in content, sidebar and mobile web.

specs.name: Leaderboard
specs.notes: Desktop header and footer slot. Keep copy short; height is tight.

specs.name: Wide Skyscraper
specs.notes: Desktop side rail. Stack logo, message and CTA vertically.

specs.name: Half Page
specs.notes: High-impact rail unit with strong viewability on most layouts.

specs.name: Billboard
specs.notes: Premium desktop top-of-page unit.

specs.name: Super Leaderboard
specs.notes: Wider leaderboard; often also the collapsed state of a pushdown.

specs.name: Large Rectangle
specs.notes: Slightly larger in-content rectangle; many sites accept 300×250 in the same slot.

specs.name: Portrait
specs.notes: Tall rail unit for long-scroll pages.

specs.name: Mobile Banner
specs.notes: Standard mobile web and in-app banner. Supply 640×100 for high-density screens.

specs.name: Large Mobile Banner
specs.notes: Taller mobile banner with room for a real headline.

specs.name: Mobile Banner (legacy)
specs.notes: Older mobile size still requested by some exchanges.

specs.name: Mobile Interstitial (portrait)
specs.notes: Full-screen in-app placement. Supply 640×960 or larger for modern devices.

specs.name: Full Banner
specs.notes: Legacy unit; low availability today.

specs.name: Square
specs.notes: Legacy unit; mostly used as a 300×250 fallback.

specs.name: Main image, landscape
specs.notes: 1.91:1. The most widely accepted native image ratio. Keep key subject centred; feeds crop differently.

specs.name: Main image, square
specs.notes: 1:1 alternative for in-feed and content recommendation widgets.

specs.name: Brand logo / icon
specs.notes: Square. Must stay legible at very small sizes.

specs.name: Headline
specs.notes: Supply a short and a long version; widgets truncate without warning.

specs.name: Body / description
specs.notes: Optional on many placements; front-load the message.

specs.name: Native video
specs.notes: 16:9 is safest; some placements prefer 1:1 or 4:5. Design for sound-off.

specs.name: In-stream, 16:9
specs.notes: Provide several bitrates. Captions recommended; a clear end card helps completion.

specs.name: Bumper (non-skippable)
specs.notes: One idea, brand in the first two seconds.

specs.name: Outstream (in-article)
specs.notes: Autoplays muted in content. Burn in captions; assume no sound.

specs.name: Vertical video, 9:16
specs.notes: Mobile-first placements. Keep text inside the centre safe zone, clear of UI overlays.

specs.name: Square video, 1:1
specs.notes: Good compromise asset when one file must run in feeds and players.

specs.name: Streaming audio spot :15
specs.notes: Name the brand early. Pair with a companion banner (often 300×250 or 640×640).

specs.name: Streaming audio spot :30
specs.notes: The standard audio length. Loudness targets vary by platform; ask for the spec sheet.

specs.name: Podcast spot :60
specs.notes: Pre-, mid- or post-roll. Host-read ads need a brief, not a file.

specs.name: Companion banner
specs.notes: Square companion shown in the player; some platforms also take 300×250.

specs.name: CTV spot :15
specs.notes: Supply a broadcast-quality mezzanine; the platform transcodes. Loudness often around −24 LKFS.

specs.name: CTV spot :30
specs.notes: No letterboxing or slates. Keep text in the title-safe area.

specs.name: CTV spot, 4K
specs.notes: Accepted by some premium publishers; 1080p is still the safe default.

specs.name: Pause ad
specs.notes: Static image shown on pause. Leave space for player UI.

specs.name: Landscape screen (HD)
specs.notes: Usually no audio. Big type, one message; viewers glance for a second or two.

specs.name: Portrait screen (HD)
specs.notes: Malls, transit and street furniture. Check the bezel and safe area.

specs.name: Digital bulletin (roadside)
specs.notes: Pixel sizes vary widely by board. Seven words or fewer; usually no motion allowed.

specs.name: Digital poster
specs.notes: Smaller roadside or urban format; sizes vary by operator.

specs.name: Feed image, 1:1
specs.notes: Works across most feeds (Meta, LinkedIn, X).

specs.name: Feed image / video, 4:5
specs.notes: Takes more mobile feed space than 1:1 on Facebook and Instagram.

specs.name: Stories / Reels, 9:16
specs.notes: Leave roughly the top and bottom 14% free of text for platform UI.

specs.name: TikTok in-feed video
specs.notes: Native-looking, sound-on creative. Keep captions clear of the right-side buttons.

specs.name: LinkedIn single image
specs.notes: 1.91:1 landscape; 1:1 also accepted.

specs.name: X (Twitter) image
specs.notes: 16:9 landscape; 1:1 also accepted.

specs.name: Pinterest standard pin
specs.notes: 2:3 vertical. Taller ratios may be cropped.

specs.name: YouTube Shorts ad
specs.notes: Vertical 9:16; served through Google Ads.

specs.name: Snapchat single image or video
specs.notes: Full-screen vertical; keep the bottom band clear for the call to action.

specs.name: Pushdown
specs.notes: Expands to around 970×415, pushing page content down rather than covering it.

specs.name: Expandable rectangle
specs.notes: Expands over content (e.g. to 600×250 or 600×500). Must include a clear close control.

specs.name: Interstitial / overlay
specs.duration: Often auto-closes after a few seconds
specs.notes: Full-screen overlays are restricted by Better Ads Standards on many sites; check placement rules.

specs.name: Mobile adhesion
specs.notes: Sticky bottom bar. Must not cover more than about 30% of the screen; include a close option.

specs.name: Site skin / takeover
specs.notes: Background artwork around the content well. Content width varies by site, so get a template.

specs.name: In-banner video
specs.notes: Video inside a display slot. User-initiated sound only.
